title: Record ESC-25: test-the-tests cannot pass a pure refactor
body:
One row appended to `docs/escapes.md`. No code.

**What escaped.** #176 retires the `FetchFailure` re-export shim from `transcripts.py` — the code half of **OD-12**, which ratified that type in `ledger.py`. It moves one import and changes no behaviour. `test-the-tests` reverts the implementation and requires the suite to go red; both trees behave identically at run time, because `from find_best_mobo.ledger import FetchFailure` still binds `transcripts.FetchFailure` as a module attribute. The only thing the change removes is mypy's explicit `X as X` re-export marking, a TYPE-level constraint no run-time test can observe. So there is no test that can satisfy the check, and a required check is permanently red on a change the oracle ordered.

**Why a row rather than a workaround.** `test-the-tests` already skips any pull request touching no file under `src/` or none under `tests/`. Splitting the refactor into a src-only pull request and a tests-only pull request would make both halves skip, legitimately, with no escape filed and no record left. That hatch is self-service — the same shape `plan-resolve.sh` closed by size-capping its exempt prefixes, still open here. The row names it so the next agent's use of it is not silent.

**This entry authorizes nothing.** The ledger says so itself: entries are records, never authorization. #176 stays red on `test-the-tests` and needs the owner to merge it past that check. Reopening it as `feat/corpus-and-checkpoint-retire-fetchfailure-shim` once this lands — that is the plan whose OD-12 paragraph orders the change, and it fixes the `plan` failure the same branch also hit.

Ran locally against this diff: `plan-resolve.sh` (exempt, 1 added line, cap 50), `escapes-append-only.sh` (8 landed rows intact), `escape-refs.sh` (10 citations, all resolve at the base).
